Automation Opportunity: - Redemption fully automated (scan → validate → apply → log); manager-override on verified-valid
Controls: - CTL-404 (ensure controlled execution — Coupon Redemption & Fraud Prevention (PA-58.2).)
- operational: redemption/liability integrity; CTL-196 (coupon & promo-code abuse prevention — fraud patterns monitored per W2249); operational: Store Manager daily-close review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Invalid-coupon-friction risk**: a valid coupon is rejected (system error, eligibility mis-check), frustrating the customer; mitigated by the manager-override on verified-valid coupons

steps.activity: Cashier scans the coupon barcode or enters the code; system validates (active, eligible SKU, min-spend met, not-expired, per-customer-limit); applies the discount; logs the redemption for vendor reconciliation and liability reduction

fields.Trigger: Customer returns item bought with coupon

Controls: - CTL-404 (ensure controlled execution — Coupon Redemption & Fraud Prevention (PA-58.2).)
- operational: coupon-reversal integrity; CTL-179 (refunds/credits issued to original tender with exception approval); operational: CS Supervisor sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Refund-abuse risk**: a customer buys with a coupon, returns, and gets a full-price refund (pocketing the coupon value); mitigated by the post-coupon-price refund policy (system-enforced)
- **Coupon-reversal-failure risk**: the coupon isn't restored on return, so the customer loses it; mitigated by the atomic return-and-coupon-reversal transaction
System Touchpoints: - Returns (links to VS-32 / W12 returns, VS-16 / W101 refund) — the return processing
- Coupon/liability (links to VS-58 / W2241, W2246) — the coupon-reversal and liability-adjustment
- Vendor reimbursement (links to VS-58 / W2242, W2253) — the vendor-funding adjustment

steps.activity: System processes the return: refunds the post-coupon price (not the full price), reverses the coupon redemption (restores the coupon if still valid, or reduces the liability if expired), adjusts the vendor reimbursement if vendor-funded

Automation Opportunity: - Grace-window auto-applied (within 7 days = auto-honor; beyond = manager-decision)
Controls: - CTL-404 (ensure controlled execution — Coupon Redemption & Fraud Prevention (PA-58.2).)
- CTL-404 (coupon-expiry authorization); operational: Store Manager sign-off on beyond-grace honors
Pain Points / Risks: - **Goodwill-abuse risk**: customers learn that expired coupons are always honored, eroding the expiry discipline; mitigated by the defined grace-window (not open-ended)
- **Inconsistent-honoring risk**: one store honors, another declines, creating a fairness perception issue; mitigated by the standardized grace-window policy
System Touchpoints: - Coupon platform (links to VS-58 / W2238) — the expiry validation
- POS (links to VS-08 / W5B) — the manager-override application
- Goodwill policy (links to VS-13 / W65 CSAT) — the customer-experience lens

steps.activity: Cashier flags the expired coupon; Store Manager decides: honor as goodwill (within a defined grace window, e.g., 7 days post-expiry), or decline; system applies if honored

Controls: - CTL-404 (ensure controlled execution — Coupon Redemption & Fraud Prevention (PA-58.2).)
- CTL-404 (coupon-binding integrity); CTL-196 (multi-account abuse prevention — links to VS-125); operational: IT Integration Lead monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Multi-account-abuse risk**: a customer creates multiple accounts to claim multiple per-customer coupons; mitigated by the device-binding (one coupon per device) and the multi-account detection
- **Binding-failure risk**: the coupon is claimed but not bound, so it doesn't appear at redemption; mitigated by the binding-confirmation
